PyTorch’s contracts suggest a decisive same-tensor test: run the GRU once, then compare the production readout with explicit indexing of that exact output tensor. For nonempty left-padded histories, select the final nonpadding position, never `count−1`; `length−1` applies only after compacting histories into valid prefixes. Exact equality between two selections of identical elements isolates indexing from floating-point computation. Before packing, compact valid tokens in chronological order; exclude empty rows and explicitly restore their defined fallback representations. Packing operates on sequence prefixes. [Packing documentation](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/generated/torch.nn.utils.rnn.pack_padded_sequence.html)

Recommended metamorphic checks: prepend padding without truncation; permute and restore batch rows; include duplicate histories, tied lengths, singleton histories and empty rows; change batch composition. Outputs should remain equivalent within numerical tolerance. Independently compare packed execution against each unpadded history processed alone using identical weights and initial states. For a unidirectional GRU, compare unpacked final-valid outputs against `h_n[-1]`. Automatic unpacking and returned hidden states restore original row order; avoid applying the inverse permutation twice. If manually sorting, invert that permutation exactly once. [GRU contract](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/generated/torch.nn.GRU.html), [implementation](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/main/torch/nn/modules/rnn.py)

Execution prerequisites: frozen checkpoint, `eval()`, disabled gradients, fixed preprocessing, initial states, device and dtype. Compare exported predictor features and candidate scores against the training implementation using identical histories, candidate IDs and ordering, including empty and mixed-length batches. Report absolute/relative errors and ranking margins; separate feature discrepancies from scoring discrepancies. Same-tensor selection failures establish a defect; cross-execution differences alone do not, because batched and individual computations need not be bitwise identical. These checks constitute a proposed diagnostic protocol, not an established novel GRU method. [Numerical accuracy](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/main/docs/source/notes/numerical_accuracy.md)
